While it is true that the ancient Hebrews did not make an image of their god, since it was forbidden to look upon his face, it is not true that they believed that only a single god existed. When the Hebrew tribes, which were nomadic, moved from place to place, the Tabernacle was struck and carried with them. That's right, when the Hebrew tribes were on the move, they put their god into a little box and carried him. This is what the Ark was actually for. When they set up the Tabernacle tent, they let their god out of the box and into the tent. Naturally, when a permanent Temple was constructed in Jerusalem to house their god, they no longer needed the little carrier box.
